        "source_locator": "source.txt:115-130",
        "source_quote": "    3. Stable assignments and a marriage problem. This situation is, of course, highly unnatural in the context\nof college admissions, but there is another \"story\" into which it fits quite\nreadily.\n    A certain community consists of n men and n women. Each person ranks\nthose of the opposite sex in accordance with his or her preferences for a marriage\npartner. We seek a satisfactory way of marrying off all members of the com-\nmunity.         "semantic_claim": "Every applicant weakly prefers the assignment returned by the deferred-acceptance procedure to every other stable assignment.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "11b3b684db63848bc65287c8ebfe6024f33e6f234fa1bd79c02b2d8ee29633e8",
        "source_locator": "source.txt:280-282",
        "source_quote": "   THEOREM 2. Every applicant is at least as well off under the assignment given\nby the deferred acceptance procedure as he would be under any other stable assign\nment.",
        "source_quote_sha256": "b816b58f2106372c658c86b2ea6af7b760d96a6868ffeb364880a9795c7954ed"
      },
      {
        "id": "theorem2.section4_top_q_procedure",
        "schema": 1,
        "semantic_claim": "Applicants apply in preference order only to mutually eligible colleges; after each batch, a quota-q college retains its top q applicants from its prior waiting list together with new applicants, and the terminal waiting lists become the assignment.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "8a89914a155c66144d123663dd6fd692e26fa04758866b54e5736aede47bc182",
        "source_locator": "source.txt:251-274",
        "source_quote": "   4. Stable assignments and the admissions problem. The extension of our\n\"deferred-acceptance\" procedure to the problem of college admissions is straight-\nforward. For convenience we will assume that if a college is not willing to accept\na student under any circumstances, as described in Section 2, then that student\nwill not even be permitted to apply to the college. With this understanding the\nprocedure follows: First, all students apply to the college of their first choice.\nA college with a quota of q then places on its waiting list the q applicants who\nrank highest, or all applicants if there are fewer than q, and rejects the rest.\nRejected applicants then apply to their second choice and again each college\nselects the top q from among the new applicants and those on its waiting list,\nputs these on its new waiting list, and rejects the rest. The procedure terminates\nwhen every applicant is either on a waiting list or has been rejected by every\ncollege to which he is willing and permitted to apply. At this point each college\n\n\n\n                                    This content downloaded from\n                  103.27.11.106 on Sun, 19 Dec 2021 14:02:55 UTC\n                            All use subject to https://about.jstor.org/terms\n\f14 COLLEGE ADMISSIONS AND STABILITY OF MARRIAGE [January\n\nadmits everyone on its waiting list and the stable assignment has been achieved.\nThe proof that the assignment is stable is entirely analogous to the proof given\nfor the marriage problem and is left to the reader.",

      }

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Every finite equal-side complete strict marriage preference profile admits a complete marriage with no mutually preferable unmatched pair.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote: THEOREM 1. There always exists a stable set of marriages.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Section 3 fixes two finite communities of the same size, has every participant rank every member of the opposite community, and seeks a marriage covering all participants.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
3. Stable assignments and a marriage problem. In trying to settle the
question of the existence of stable assignments we were led to look first at a
special case, in which there are the same number of applicants as colleges and all
quotas are unity. This situation is, of course, highly unnatural in the context
of college admissions, but there is another "story" into which it fits quite
readily.
    A certain community consists of n men and n women. Each person ranks
those of the opposite sex in accordance with his or her preferences for a marriage
partner. We seek a satisfactory way of marrying off all members of the com-
munity. Imitating our earlier definition, we call a set of marriages unstable (and
here the suitability of the term is quite clear) if under it there are a man and a
woman who are not married to each other but prefer each other to their actual
mates.

   QUESTION: For any pattern of preferences is it possible to find a stable set of
marriages?

source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
4. Stable assignments and the admissions problem. The extension of our
"deferred-acceptance" procedure to the problem of college admissions is straight-
forward. For convenience we will assume that if a college is not willing to accept
a student under any circumstances, as described in Section 2, then that student
will not even be permitted to apply to the college. With this understanding the
procedure follows: First, all students apply to the college of their first choice.
A college with a quota of q then places on its waiting list the q applicants who
rank highest, or all applicants if there are fewer than q, and rejects the rest.
Rejected applicants then apply to their second choice and again each college
selects the top q from among the new applicants and those on its waiting list,
puts these on its new waiting list, and rejects the rest. The procedure terminates
when every applicant is either on a waiting list or has been rejected by every
college to which he is willing and permitted to apply. At this point each college

Neither definition silently receives individual rationality, a vacant-seat block, or an unmatched-applicant block.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This checks the two printed definitions literally. The completed standard-stability predicate needed by the general Section 4 and Theorem 2 route is kept distinct and is governed by GS62-LITERAL-STABILITY-COMPLETION-01.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Define college-assignment instability by a currently assigned applicant replacing another currently assigned applicant at a mutually preferred college, and define applicant optimality by weak comparison with every stable assignment.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For distinct finite side types of equal cardinality, every complete strict preference profile has a complete assignment with no man-woman pair who both strictly prefer one another to their assigned mates.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The theorem exposes equal cardinality and the complete strict domain in its type. It does not obtain the result from a same-carrier specialization or from the spelling of a stability predicate.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Run proposer-side deferred acceptance on two finite equally sized communities with complete strict preferences, then use the fact that a rejected proposal was displaced by a more preferred proposal to rule out a blocking pair at termination.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The direct state records cumulative applications, proves that each round's waiting list equals top-q of old holders union new applicants, preserves disjoint waiting lists and best-first application history, and strictly decreases the finite set of eligible untried pairs whenever an applicant remains active.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This repairs a prior formalization-only audit finding. The earlier cloned-seat sequential stage runner had not been shown to realize the source's within-batch top-q state evolution and could allow a displaced applicant to reapply in a later stage. The published Section 4 algorithm is not classified as defective: source-facing credit now uses the direct exact runner, while cloned-seat machinery is auxiliary comparison support only.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: In each batch, every unmatched applicant with an untried mutually eligible college applies to the best such college, and each college retains exactly its top quota-many applicants from its previous waiting list together with that batch's new applicants.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The finite untried-pair measure proves termination. At the terminal state the induced assignment is consistent, respects every quota, assigns only mutually acceptable pairs, and has no applicant-college block through either a vacancy or replacement of a lower-ranked assignee.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This proves the Section 4 runner's completed-standard stability directly from its state invariants and terminal condition. Standard stability then implies the separately preserved literal no-replacement condition.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Terminate when every applicant is either held on one waiting list or has exhausted every willing and permitted application, and admit exactly the terminal waiting lists.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Every rejected applicant-college pair is impossible in every completed-standard stable assignment, and every applicant weakly prefers the exact terminal waiting-list assignment to that applicant's match in every other completed-standard stable assignment.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The argument starts from the finite strict-list market and the direct source runner, derives the rejection invariant internally, and accepts no possible-college certificate, stable comparison outcome, or optimality conclusion from the caller. Equality with the reusable applicant-proposing assignment is proved afterward from the independently established applicant-optimal stable characterizations.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Induct over applications and rejections to show that whenever a college rejects an applicant, no completed-standard stable assignment can match that applicant to that college; use this rejection invariant to compare the terminal assignment with an arbitrary stable assignment.

defects.acceptance_condition: Lean proves the literal definition and a strict-domain boundary assignment that is literal-stable but not completed-standard stable, proves completed stability implies the literal condition, and proves the exact top-q waiting-list output is completed-standard stable and weakly applicant-dominates every completed-standard stable assignment.
defects.repair_obligation: Formalize the displayed replacement-pair definition literally; distinguish it from feasible, individually rational many-to-one stability with both vacancy and replacement blocks; exhibit that the literal predicate alone is insufficient on an unmatched-applicant boundary; and prove the Section 4 runner stable and applicant-optimal against the completed comparison class without assuming the two predicates are generally equivalent.
defects.resolution_evidence: SourceStability.lean gives separate literal and completed predicates, proves the one-way implication, and checks a one-college one-seat two-applicant strict-domain witness that the literal predicate accepts although the unmatched higher-ranked applicant blocks. ExactCollegeBatchedProcedure.lean derives quota feasibility, two-sided individual rationality, absence of vacancy/replacement blocks, the rejection-impossibility invariant, and applicant optimality for the direct top-q terminal assignment. PaperInterface.lean exposes the two literal definition Specs and the completed Theorem 2 Spec separately, so no predicate name or hidden equivalence supplies the repair.
defects.source_claim: The paper first defines an unstable college assignment only through a replacement pair involving two currently assigned applicants, but Section 4 calls its arbitrary-quota waiting-list outcome stable and Theorem 2 compares that outcome with every stable assignment.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The isolated page-10 predicate omits individual rationality, vacancy blocks, and blocks by an unmatched applicant, so it is too weak as the comparison class for the general arbitrary-quota proof. This is a local implicit-completion issue rather than a change to the advertised deferred-acceptance result: the source proof uses the ordinary completed blocking-pair semantics, and Lean proves that exact completed theorem while retaining the literal displayed definition separately. The paper therefore remains plain formalized, with a note rather than a caveat.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem 1 uses the positive complete-list encoding. The displayed college definitions and Theorem 2 use the incomplete-list encoding with zero as unmatched. The direct Section 4 runner filters to mutually positive pairs before choosing an application, and completed stability excludes assignment to a negative pair, so no paper-facing conclusion assigns source meaning to the relative order among omitted alternatives.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Lean represents each finite strict preference list by a nonzero injective real-valued score with zero as the outside option. In the complete marriage model every opposite-side participant is acceptable and receives a positive score. In the college model a positive score means listed and acceptable, while omitted alternatives receive arbitrary distinct negative scores solely to make the numerical function total.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses finite ordered lists, including incomplete lists in the college model, whereas the reusable matching API takes total real-valued functions. The sign convention preserves acceptability and the score order preserves every listed ranking; making the arbitrary order among omitted negative alternatives explicit prevents that Lean-only totalization from being mistaken for additional source preference data.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The exact waiting-list state exposes only mutually eligible untried colleges to an active applicant. Every new application satisfies the two-sided sign test, and the terminal stability and applicant-optimality results require only the strict-list domain; they have no global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: An applicant-college pair is eligible for the Section 4 procedure exactly when the applicant lists the college as acceptable and the college has not eliminated the applicant as unacceptable. In the numerical representation this is the pairwise conjunction of a positive applicant score and a positive college score.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source separately permits applicants to omit colleges they would never attend and forbids applications to colleges that would never admit the applicant. This is a filter on each possible application, not a global assumption that every college acceptable to an applicant must accept that applicant. Recording the pairwise rule prevents the earlier global implication from being smuggled into Theorem 2.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Every finite equal-side complete strict marriage preference profile admits a complete marriage with no mutually preferable unmatched pair.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote: THEOREM 1. There always exists a stable set of marriages.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Section 3 fixes two finite communities of the same size, has every participant rank every member of the opposite community, and seeks a marriage covering all participants.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
3. Stable assignments and a marriage problem. In trying to settle the
question of the existence of stable assignments we were led to look first at a
special case, in which there are the same number of applicants as colleges and all
quotas are unity. This situation is, of course, highly unnatural in the context
of college admissions, but there is another "story" into which it fits quite
readily.
    A certain community consists of n men and n women. Each person ranks
those of the opposite sex in accordance with his or her preferences for a marriage
partner. We seek a satisfactory way of marrying off all members of the com-
munity. Imitating our earlier definition, we call a set of marriages unstable (and
here the suitability of the term is quite clear) if under it there are a man and a
woman who are not married to each other but prefer each other to their actual
mates.

   QUESTION: For any pattern of preferences is it possible to find a stable set of
marriages?

THEOREM 2. Every applicant is at least as well off under the assignment given

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Applicants apply in preference order only to mutually eligible colleges; after each batch, a quota-q college retains its top q applicants from its prior waiting list together with new applicants, and the terminal waiting lists become the assignment.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
4. Stable assignments and the admissions problem. The extension of our
"deferred-acceptance" procedure to the problem of college admissions is straight-
forward. For convenience we will assume that if a college is not willing to accept
a student under any circumstances, as described in Section 2, then that student
will not even be permitted to apply to the college. With this understanding the
procedure follows: First, all students apply to the college of their first choice.
A college with a quota of q then places on its waiting list the q applicants who
rank highest, or all applicants if there are fewer than q, and rejects the rest.
Rejected applicants then apply to their second choice and again each college
selects the top q from among the new applicants and those on its waiting list,
puts these on its new waiting list, and rejects the rest. The procedure terminates
when every applicant is either on a waiting list or has been rejected by every
college to which he is willing and permitted to apply. At this point each college

Neither definition silently receives individual rationality, a vacant-seat block, or an unmatched-applicant block.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This checks the two printed definitions literally. The completed standard-stability predicate needed by the general Section 4 and Theorem 2 route is kept distinct and is governed by GS62-LITERAL-STABILITY-COMPLETION-01.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Define college-assignment instability by a currently assigned applicant replacing another currently assigned applicant at a mutually preferred college, and define applicant optimality by weak comparison with every stable assignment.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For distinct finite side types of equal cardinality, every complete strict preference profile has a complete assignment with no man-woman pair who both strictly prefer one another to their assigned mates.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The theorem exposes equal cardinality and the complete strict domain in its type. It does not obtain the result from a same-carrier specialization or from the spelling of a stability predicate.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Run proposer-side deferred acceptance on two finite equally sized communities with complete strict preferences, then use the fact that a rejected proposal was displaced by a more preferred proposal to rule out a blocking pair at termination.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The direct state records cumulative applications, proves that each round's waiting list equals top-q of old holders union new applicants, preserves disjoint waiting lists and best-first application history, and strictly decreases the finite set of eligible untried pairs whenever an applicant remains active.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This repairs a prior formalization-only audit finding. The earlier cloned-seat sequential stage runner had not been shown to realize the source's within-batch top-q state evolution and could allow a displaced applicant to reapply in a later stage. The published Section 4 algorithm is not classified as defective: source-facing credit now uses the direct exact runner, while cloned-seat machinery is auxiliary comparison support only.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: In each batch, every unmatched applicant with an untried mutually eligible college applies to the best such college, and each college retains exactly its top quota-many applicants from its previous waiting list together with that batch's new applicants.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The finite untried-pair measure proves termination. At the terminal state the induced assignment is consistent, respects every quota, assigns only mutually acceptable pairs, and has no applicant-college block through either a vacancy or replacement of a lower-ranked assignee.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This proves the Section 4 runner's completed-standard stability directly from its state invariants and terminal condition. Standard stability then implies the separately preserved literal no-replacement condition.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Terminate when every applicant is either held on one waiting list or has exhausted every willing and permitted application, and admit exactly the terminal waiting lists.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Every rejected applicant-college pair is impossible in every completed-standard stable assignment, and every applicant weakly prefers the exact terminal waiting-list assignment to that applicant's match in every other completed-standard stable assignment.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The argument starts from the finite strict-list market and the direct source runner, derives the rejection invariant internally, and accepts no possible-college certificate, stable comparison outcome, or optimality conclusion from the caller. Equality with the reusable applicant-proposing assignment is proved afterward from the independently established applicant-optimal stable characterizations.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Induct over applications and rejections to show that whenever a college rejects an applicant, no completed-standard stable assignment can match that applicant to that college; use this rejection invariant to compare the terminal assignment with an arbitrary stable assignment.

defects.acceptance_condition: Lean proves the literal definition and a strict-domain boundary assignment that is literal-stable but not completed-standard stable, proves completed stability implies the literal condition, and proves the exact top-q waiting-list output is completed-standard stable and weakly applicant-dominates every completed-standard stable assignment.
defects.repair_obligation: Formalize the displayed replacement-pair definition literally; distinguish it from feasible, individually rational many-to-one stability with both vacancy and replacement blocks; exhibit that the literal predicate alone is insufficient on an unmatched-applicant boundary; and prove the Section 4 runner stable and applicant-optimal against the completed comparison class without assuming the two predicates are generally equivalent.
defects.resolution_evidence: SourceStability.lean gives separate literal and completed predicates, proves the one-way implication, and checks a one-college one-seat two-applicant strict-domain witness that the literal predicate accepts although the unmatched higher-ranked applicant blocks. ExactCollegeBatchedProcedure.lean derives quota feasibility, two-sided individual rationality, absence of vacancy/replacement blocks, the rejection-impossibility invariant, and applicant optimality for the direct top-q terminal assignment. PaperInterface.lean exposes the two literal definition Specs and the completed Theorem 2 Spec separately, so no predicate name or hidden equivalence supplies the repair.
defects.source_claim: The paper first defines an unstable college assignment only through a replacement pair involving two currently assigned applicants, but Section 4 calls its arbitrary-quota waiting-list outcome stable and Theorem 2 compares that outcome with every stable assignment.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The isolated page-10 predicate omits individual rationality, vacancy blocks, and blocks by an unmatched applicant, so it is too weak as the comparison class for the general arbitrary-quota proof. This is a local implicit-completion issue rather than a change to the advertised deferred-acceptance result: the source proof uses the ordinary completed blocking-pair semantics, and Lean proves that exact completed theorem while retaining the literal displayed definition separately. The paper therefore remains plain formalized, with a note rather than a caveat.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem 1 uses the positive complete-list encoding. The displayed college definitions and Theorem 2 use the incomplete-list encoding with zero as unmatched. The direct Section 4 runner filters to mutually positive pairs before choosing an application, and completed stability excludes assignment to a negative pair, so no paper-facing conclusion assigns source meaning to the relative order among omitted alternatives.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Lean represents each finite strict preference list by a nonzero injective real-valued score with zero as the outside option. In the complete marriage model every opposite-side participant is acceptable and receives a positive score. In the college model a positive score means listed and acceptable, while omitted alternatives receive arbitrary distinct negative scores solely to make the numerical function total.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses finite ordered lists, including incomplete lists in the college model, whereas the reusable matching API takes total real-valued functions. The sign convention preserves acceptability and the score order preserves every listed ranking; making the arbitrary order among omitted negative alternatives explicit prevents that Lean-only totalization from being mistaken for additional source preference data.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The exact waiting-list state exposes only mutually eligible untried colleges to an active applicant. Every new application satisfies the two-sided sign test, and the terminal stability and applicant-optimality results require only the strict-list domain; they have no global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: An applicant-college pair is eligible for the Section 4 procedure exactly when the applicant lists the college as acceptable and the college has not eliminated the applicant as unacceptable. In the numerical representation this is the pairwise conjunction of a positive applicant score and a positive college score.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source separately permits applicants to omit colleges they would never attend and forbids applications to colleges that would never admit the applicant. This is a filter on each possible application, not a global assumption that every college acceptable to an applicant must accept that applicant. Recording the pairwise rule prevents the earlier global implication from being smuggled into Theorem 2.

The finite equal-size complete marriage domain, the prose blocking-pair definition of an unstable set of marriages, and Theorem 1's stable-marriage existence conclusion.
Theorem 1's batched proposer procedure, finite termination argument, complete terminal matching, and rejection-based proof that the terminal marriage has no mutually preferable unmatched pair.

The arbitrary-quota college procedure: mutually eligible applications in applicant preference order, simultaneous new applications by rejected applicants, exact top-q waiting-list updates, finite termination, and stability of the terminal waiting lists.

expanded_shape_basis: expanded binder/result type surface
dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

expanded_shape_basis: generic, finite, subtype, or opaque carrier surface
dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
3. Stable assignments and a marriage problem. In trying to settle the
question of the existence of stable assignments we were led to look first at a
special case, in which there are the same number of applicants as colleges and all
quotas are unity. This situation is, of course, highly unnatural in the context
of college admissions, but there is another "story" into which it fits quite
readily.
    A certain community consists of n men and n women. Each person ranks
those of the opposite sex in accordance with his or her preferences for a marriage
partner. We seek a satisfactory way of marrying off all members of the com-
munity. Imitating our earlier definition, we call a set of marriages unstable (and
here the suitability of the term is quite clear) if under it there are a man and a
woman who are not married to each other but prefer each other to their actual
mates.

   QUESTION: For any pattern of preferences is it possible to find a stable set of
marriages?

source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
4. Stable assignments and the admissions problem. The extension of our
"deferred-acceptance" procedure to the problem of college admissions is straight-
forward. For convenience we will assume that if a college is not willing to accept
a student under any circumstances, as described in Section 2, then that student
will not even be permitted to apply to the college. With this understanding the
procedure follows: First, all students apply to the college of their first choice.
A college with a quota of q then places on its waiting list the q applicants who
rank highest, or all applicants if there are fewer than q, and rejects the rest.
Rejected applicants then apply to their second choice and again each college
selects the top q from among the new applicants and those on its waiting list,
puts these on its new waiting list, and rejects the rest. The procedure terminates
when every applicant is either on a waiting list or has been rejected by every
college to which he is willing and permitted to apply. At this point each college

Neither definition silently receives individual rationality, a vacant-seat block, or an unmatched-applicant block.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This checks the two printed definitions literally. The completed standard-stability predicate needed by the general Section 4 and Theorem 2 route is kept distinct and is governed by GS62-LITERAL-STABILITY-COMPLETION-01.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Define college-assignment instability by a currently assigned applicant replacing another currently assigned applicant at a mutually preferred college, and define applicant optimality by weak comparison with every stable assignment.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For distinct finite side types of equal cardinality, every complete strict preference profile has a complete assignment with no man-woman pair who both strictly prefer one another to their assigned mates.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The theorem exposes equal cardinality and the complete strict domain in its type. It does not obtain the result from a same-carrier specialization or from the spelling of a stability predicate.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Run proposer-side deferred acceptance on two finite equally sized communities with complete strict preferences, then use the fact that a rejected proposal was displaced by a more preferred proposal to rule out a blocking pair at termination.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The direct state records cumulative applications, proves that each round's waiting list equals top-q of old holders union new applicants, preserves disjoint waiting lists and best-first application history, and strictly decreases the finite set of eligible untried pairs whenever an applicant remains active.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This repairs a prior formalization-only audit finding. The earlier cloned-seat sequential stage runner had not been shown to realize the source's within-batch top-q state evolution and could allow a displaced applicant to reapply in a later stage. The published Section 4 algorithm is not classified as defective: source-facing credit now uses the direct exact runner, while cloned-seat machinery is auxiliary comparison support only.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: In each batch, every unmatched applicant with an untried mutually eligible college applies to the best such college, and each college retains exactly its top quota-many applicants from its previous waiting list together with that batch's new applicants.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The finite untried-pair measure proves termination. At the terminal state the induced assignment is consistent, respects every quota, assigns only mutually acceptable pairs, and has no applicant-college block through either a vacancy or replacement of a lower-ranked assignee.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This proves the Section 4 runner's completed-standard stability directly from its state invariants and terminal condition. Standard stability then implies the separately preserved literal no-replacement condition.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Terminate when every applicant is either held on one waiting list or has exhausted every willing and permitted application, and admit exactly the terminal waiting lists.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Every rejected applicant-college pair is impossible in every completed-standard stable assignment, and every applicant weakly prefers the exact terminal waiting-list assignment to that applicant's match in every other completed-standard stable assignment.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The argument starts from the finite strict-list market and the direct source runner, derives the rejection invariant internally, and accepts no possible-college certificate, stable comparison outcome, or optimality conclusion from the caller. Equality with the reusable applicant-proposing assignment is proved afterward from the independently established applicant-optimal stable characterizations.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Induct over applications and rejections to show that whenever a college rejects an applicant, no completed-standard stable assignment can match that applicant to that college; use this rejection invariant to compare the terminal assignment with an arbitrary stable assignment.

defects.acceptance_condition: Lean proves the literal definition and a strict-domain boundary assignment that is literal-stable but not completed-standard stable, proves completed stability implies the literal condition, and proves the exact top-q waiting-list output is completed-standard stable and weakly applicant-dominates every completed-standard stable assignment.
defects.repair_obligation: Formalize the displayed replacement-pair definition literally; distinguish it from feasible, individually rational many-to-one stability with both vacancy and replacement blocks; exhibit that the literal predicate alone is insufficient on an unmatched-applicant boundary; and prove the Section 4 runner stable and applicant-optimal against the completed comparison class without assuming the two predicates are generally equivalent.
defects.resolution_evidence: SourceStability.lean gives separate literal and completed predicates, proves the one-way implication, and checks a one-college one-seat two-applicant strict-domain witness that the literal predicate accepts although the unmatched higher-ranked applicant blocks. ExactCollegeBatchedProcedure.lean derives quota feasibility, two-sided individual rationality, absence of vacancy/replacement blocks, the rejection-impossibility invariant, and applicant optimality for the direct top-q terminal assignment. PaperInterface.lean exposes the two literal definition Specs and the completed Theorem 2 Spec separately, so no predicate name or hidden equivalence supplies the repair.
defects.source_claim: The paper first defines an unstable college assignment only through a replacement pair involving two currently assigned applicants, but Section 4 calls its arbitrary-quota waiting-list outcome stable and Theorem 2 compares that outcome with every stable assignment.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The isolated page-10 predicate omits individual rationality, vacancy blocks, and blocks by an unmatched applicant, so it is too weak as the comparison class for the general arbitrary-quota proof. This is a local implicit-completion issue rather than a change to the advertised deferred-acceptance result: the source proof uses the ordinary completed blocking-pair semantics, and Lean proves that exact completed theorem while retaining the literal displayed definition separately. The paper therefore remains plain formalized, with a note rather than a caveat.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem 1 uses the positive complete-list encoding. The displayed college definitions and Theorem 2 use the incomplete-list encoding with zero as unmatched. The direct Section 4 runner filters to mutually positive pairs before choosing an application, and completed stability excludes assignment to a negative pair, so no paper-facing conclusion assigns source meaning to the relative order among omitted alternatives.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Lean represents each finite strict preference list by a nonzero injective real-valued score with zero as the outside option. In the complete marriage model every opposite-side participant is acceptable and receives a positive score. In the college model a positive score means listed and acceptable, while omitted alternatives receive arbitrary distinct negative scores solely to make the numerical function total.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses finite ordered lists, including incomplete lists in the college model, whereas the reusable matching API takes total real-valued functions. The sign convention preserves acceptability and the score order preserves every listed ranking; making the arbitrary order among omitted negative alternatives explicit prevents that Lean-only totalization from being mistaken for additional source preference data.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The exact waiting-list state exposes only mutually eligible untried colleges to an active applicant. Every new application satisfies the two-sided sign test, and the terminal stability and applicant-optimality results require only the strict-list domain; they have no global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: An applicant-college pair is eligible for the Section 4 procedure exactly when the applicant lists the college as acceptable and the college has not eliminated the applicant as unacceptable. In the numerical representation this is the pairwise conjunction of a positive applicant score and a positive college score.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source separately permits applicants to omit colleges they would never attend and forbids applications to colleges that would never admit the applicant. This is a filter on each possible application, not a global assumption that every college acceptable to an applicant must accept that applicant. Recording the pairwise rule prevents the earlier global implication from being smuggled into Theorem 2.

reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: The Section 2 finite strict college-admissions domain, unacceptable alternatives, quotas, the displayed replacement-pair definition of instability, and the displayed applicant-optimality definition over stable assignments.
The finite equal-size complete marriage domain, the prose blocking-pair definition of an unstable set of marriages, and Theorem 1's stable-marriage existence conclusion.
Theorem 1's batched proposer procedure, finite termination argument, complete terminal matching, and rejection-based proof that the terminal marriage has no mutually preferable unmatched pair.

The arbitrary-quota college procedure: mutually eligible applications in applicant preference order, simultaneous new applications by rejected applicants, exact top-q waiting-list updates, finite termination, and stability of the terminal waiting lists.
Theorem 2's comparison of the applicant-proposing procedure with every stable assignment and the induction showing that a rejected applicant-college pair cannot occur in any stable assignment.
